concerns.text: FR-008 and US-4 in spec.md mandate generating a 'Prompt-Based Cohort' of synthetic code to validate causal claims. tasks.md explicitly removes all generation tasks (T014b, T033) and replaces them with a 'Classifier-Based Proxy' (T033a) analyzing existing human code. This is a semantic weakening of the requirement: the task deliverable (classification of existing data) does not satisfy the spec's demand for a generated synthetic cohort, leaving FR-008 unimplemented.

FR-004 mandates that the system MUST 'fail the matching step and report an error' if covariate balance (SMD) exceeds 0.1 after 3 retries. tasks.md marks T022b (the failure reporting task) as 'REMOVED' and T023b as incomplete. No task exists to generate the mandatory failure artifact or halt the pipeline, violating the spec's error handling requirement.

SC-005 requires sensitivity analysis to report consistency if p < 0.05 in ≥ 80% of subsets. tasks.md marks T030 (which implements this check and outputs sensitivity_summary.json) as incomplete/missing. No alternative task exists to generate the required JSON evidence or perform the 80% threshold calculation, leaving SC-005 unverified.

Spec FR-002 and SC-007 require generating synthetic code with specific constraints (generation time ≤ 30s, syntax validity ≥ 95%). tasks.md removes all generation tasks (T014b, T019) and replaces them with classification. Consequently, there is no task to measure generation time or validate the syntax of generated code, making SC-007 and the generation time constraint impossible to verify or satisfy.

FR-009 requires computing semantic similarity scores to be used as a covariate in matching. The plan and tasks.md (T022) explicitly exclude semantic similarity from matching covariates to avoid collider bias. While the plan justifies this as a 'Methodological Shift', tasks.md T017b is marked 'DIAGNOSTIC ONLY' and the output file is missing, meaning the requirement to 'compute a semantic similarity score... for every code snippet' (FR-009) is technically unimplemented as a runnable, verified step for the intended purpose.
